flashcards.q: Why does the kernel trick work for SVM specifically (not any algorithm)?
flashcards.a: The dual formulation's objective and decision function depend on training data only through pairwise dot products x_i.x_j -- any K(x_i,x_j) computing a valid dot product in an implicit feature space can be substituted without ever materializing that space.

flashcards.q: SVM soft-margin C: what does large vs small C do?
flashcards.a: Large C: heavily penalizes margin violations -> narrow margin, tighter fit, lower bias/higher variance. Small C: tolerates more violations -> wide margin, higher bias/lower variance. Same tradeoff shape as ridge/lasso lambda, opposite parameterization direction.

flashcards.q: Curse of dimensionality for kNN, the actual quantitative statement?
flashcards.a: (dist_to_farthest - dist_to_nearest)/dist_to_nearest -> 0 as dimensionality grows (Beyer et al. 1999) -- nearest and farthest points become approximately equidistant, so 'nearest neighbor' loses discriminative meaning.

flashcards.q: Naive Bayes: what's the independence assumption and why does it work despite being false?
flashcards.a: P(x|y) = product_i P(x_i|y). Almost never literally true, but the bias it introduces buys large variance reduction -- estimating d one-dimensional distributions needs far less data than the full joint, and correct argmax classification is a weaker requirement than correct calibrated probabilities.

flashcards.q: Why is k-means guaranteed to converge but only to a local optimum, and what's the standard fix?
flashcards.a: Within-cluster sum of squares strictly decreases each Lloyd's-algorithm iteration and is bounded below by zero, but the objective is non-convex in assignment+centroid jointly, so different inits reach different local optima. Fix: k-means++ initialization plus multiple random restarts (n_init), keeping the best by WCSS.

flashcards.q: DBSCAN core point definition and what happens to non-cluster points?
flashcards.a: A core point has >= min_samples points within radius eps. Clusters are sets density-reachable from a core point; points reachable from no core point are labeled NOISE, not forced into the nearest cluster -- unlike k-means, which must assign every point.

flashcards.q: PCA eigendecomposition vs SVD -- why is SVD preferred in implementations?
flashcards.a: For centered X, X^TX = VS^2V^T (SVD X=USV^T) is exactly PCA's eigendecomposition. SVD is preferred because computing X^TX explicitly squares the data's condition number, amplifying numerical error -- SVD avoids forming X^TX at all.

flashcards.q: Why can't PCA capture nonlinear manifold structure regardless of components retained?
flashcards.a: PCA is strictly linear -- it can only rotate/project the original feature space. A curved manifold (e.g. a swiss roll) is fundamentally invisible to any number of linear projections.

flashcards.q: Why is it wrong to read cluster separation directly off a UMAP or t-SNE plot?
flashcards.a: Both optimize for preserving LOCAL neighborhood structure, not global pairwise distances -- nothing constrains between-cluster gaps to reflect true separation, so they can be arbitrarily stretched or compressed without violating the actual optimization objective. UMAP defaults: n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1.

flashcards.q: Why is Naive Bayes calibration typically worse than logistic regression's, even at similar accuracy?
flashcards.a: Independence assumption multiplies correlated evidence as if independent, pushing posteriors toward 0/1 more than warranted. Logistic regression directly optimizes cross-entropy on its own output probabilities, so it's comparatively better-calibrated out of the box. Accuracy parity does not imply calibration parity.
